prompt.adult: Jesus said that whoever comes to Him will never hunger. What did He call Himself?
prompt.child: Jesus said that anyone who comes to Him will never be hungry. What did He call Himself?
prompt.teen: In John 6:35, Jesus promised that those who come to Him would never go hungry. What did He say He is?
prompt.older: In John 6:35, what does Jesus declare Himself to be?

verses.text: And Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. He who comes to Me shall never hunger, and he who believes in Me shall never thirst.

explanation.adult: John 6:35 begins with Jesus' words "I am." Read what follows.
explanation.child: Find the words "I am" in John 6:35 and read the next words.
explanation.teen: Jesus' saying comes first in 6:35; the promise about hunger comes after it.
explanation.older: The predicate following "I am" in 6:35 fits the promise about hunger that follows.

teaching.extended_explanation: Jesus used something people need every day to describe what He gives. John 6:35 states the saying first and then the promise to those who come to Him. Read the words after "I am."
teaching.takeaway: Jesus said, "I am the bread of life."

prompt.adult: Jesus said that whoever follows Him will not walk in darkness. What did He call Himself?
prompt.child: Jesus said people who follow Him won't walk in the dark. What did He say He is?
prompt.teen: According to John 8:12, what did Jesus say He is, so that His followers would not walk in darkness?
prompt.older: In John 8:12, what title does Jesus claim for Himself?

verses.text: Then Jesus spoke to them again, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows Me shall not walk in darkness, but have the light of life.”

explanation.adult: Read the words right after "I am" in John 8:12.
explanation.child: Look for "I am" in John 8:12 and read the next words.
explanation.teen: 8:12 gives the saying first, then the promise about darkness.
explanation.older: The saying in 8:12 is matched by its closing promise to the one who follows.

teaching.extended_explanation: Jesus contrasted walking in darkness with following Him. John 8:12 gives His saying and then His promise to those who follow. Read the words after "I am."
teaching.takeaway: Jesus said, "I am the light of the world."

prompt.adult: Jesus compared Himself to someone who cares for sheep. What did He call Himself in John 10:11?
prompt.child: Jesus talked about Himself as someone who takes care of sheep. What did He call Himself?
prompt.teen: In John 10:11, Jesus uses a picture from caring for a flock. What does He call Himself?
prompt.older: According to John 10:11, what does Jesus say He is?

choices.text: The keeper of the city gate

verses.text: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd gives His life for the sheep.

explanation.adult: John 10:11 begins with Jesus' words "I am." Read the next three words.
explanation.child: Read the first sentence of John 10:11.
explanation.teen: The saying appears in the first sentence of 10:11 and is repeated at the start of the second.
explanation.older: The title appears twice in 10:11; the second sentence describes what that One does for the sheep.

teaching.extended_explanation: Jesus described Himself with a picture His listeners knew well from fields and flocks. Read the first sentence of John 10:11.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus said, "I am the good shepherd."

prompt.adult: In John 11:25, Jesus made a promise to everyone who believes in Him. What did He say He is?
prompt.child: Jesus said something important about Himself and about life after death. What did He say He is?
prompt.teen: John 11:25 records one of Jesus' "I am" sayings, followed by a promise to those who believe. What does He say He is?
prompt.older: According to John 11:25, what did Jesus declare Himself to be?

choices.text: The prophet who was promised long ago

verses.text: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in Me, though he may die, he shall live.

explanation.adult: Read the words that follow "I am" in John 11:25.
explanation.child: Find "I am" in John 11:25. Read the words that come after it.
explanation.teen: The saying ends before the promise "He who believes in Me."
explanation.older: The saying precedes the promise in 11:25 that the believer, though he may die, shall live.

teaching.extended_explanation: Jesus' saying in John 11:25 is followed by a promise: whoever believes in Him will live, even though he may die. Read the words after "I am" to find what Jesus said about Himself.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus said, "I am the resurrection and the life."

prompt.adult: Jesus said no one comes to the Father except through Him. What three things did He say He is?
prompt.child: Jesus said the only path to God the Father is through Him. What did He say He is?
prompt.teen: In John 14:6, Jesus answers a question with three titles for Himself. What are they?
prompt.older: According to John 14:6, what does Jesus say He is, before stating that no one comes to the Father except through Him?

choices.text: The way, the truth, and the life
The judge, the priest, and the king
The rock, the shield, and the fortress
The word, the wisdom, and the power

verses.text: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.

explanation.adult: John 14:6 lists three things after "I am." Read them in order.
explanation.child: Look for "I am" in John 14:6. Read the three things that come next.
explanation.teen: The saying in 14:6 has three parts, followed by a sentence about coming to the Father.
explanation.older: The triple predicate after "I am" in 14:6 precedes the exclusive claim about access to the Father.

teaching.extended_explanation: Jesus said that coming to the Father happens only through Him. In the same verse He describes Himself with three titles. Read the words after "I am" in John 14:6.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus said, "I am the way, the truth, and the life."

prompt.adult: Jesus said His Father is the vinedresser. What did Jesus call Himself?
prompt.child: Jesus compared His Father to a gardener who takes care of a plant. What plant did Jesus say He is?
prompt.teen: In John 15:1, Jesus describes Himself and His Father using a picture from a vineyard. What does He call Himself?
prompt.older: According to John 15:1, what does Jesus say He is, with His Father as the vinedresser?

choices.text: The fig tree by the road

verses.text: “I am the true vine, and My Father is the vinedresser.

explanation.adult: John 15:1 begins with "I am." Read the words that follow.
explanation.child: Read the first part of John 15:1.
explanation.teen: 15:1 has two parts: what Jesus is, then what His Father is. You need the first.
explanation.older: The first clause of 15:1 names Jesus; the second names the Father's role.

teaching.extended_explanation: Jesus used a picture of a growing plant cared for by a gardener. John 15:1 names Jesus' part and His Father's part. Read the first half of the verse.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus said, "I am the true vine, and My Father is the vinedresser."

prompt.teen: According to John 10:11, what is given for the sheep?
prompt.older: John 10:11 describes a costly gift made for the sheep. What is it?

verses.text: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd gives His life for the sheep.

explanation.adult: Read the second sentence of John 10:11. It says what is given for the sheep.
explanation.child: Look at the second sentence of John 10:11.

prompt.adult: In John 6:35, Jesus pairs coming to Him with never hungering. What does He pair with believing in Him?
prompt.child: Jesus said that people who come to Him will never be hungry. What did He say about people who believe in Him?
prompt.teen: John 6:35 has two matching promises. The first is about coming and hunger. What is the second promise to those who believe?
prompt.older: John 6:35 sets two promises side by side. How does the second, for the one who believes, complete the picture of the first?

verses.text: And Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. He who comes to Me shall never hunger, and he who believes in Me shall never thirst.

explanation.adult: John 6:35 has two matching lines. Read the second one, which begins "he who believes in Me."
explanation.teen: Line up the two promises in 6:35. The second ends with the answer.
explanation.older: 6:35 uses parallelism: coming matches believing, and hunger matches a related need. Read the final clause.

teaching.extended_explanation: Jesus called Himself the source of what people truly need. In John 6:35 He gives two promises that mirror each other, one for those who come to Him and one for those who believe in Him. Read the second promise.
teaching.takeaway: Whoever believes in Jesus shall never thirst.
